subject: physical-education
successCriteria: The learner holds organizing an activity that includes mixed abilities by design by leading one safely available participant or rehearsing a complete written leadership plan that resolves the same disagreement or mixed-ability problem, in whatever version their body and setting allow. Full transfer credit requires the opening directions, adaptation, feedback, conflict response, and stop signal for the segment. Live leadership or a complete written and rehearsed plan earns equal credit when it preserves each leadership decision; leading a group is not required.
The learner names what degraded first and why, rather than reporting only whether it worked.
The learner compares this occasion with the earlier one and says what actually changed.
scoringGuidance: Score safe participation, skill cues, tactical reasoning, self-management, and revision. Accept any version of the task the learner’s body and setting allow as full credit when it supplies the stated transfer evidence. Never score body size, weight, body composition, appearance, speed alone, or comparison with another person. Full transfer credit requires the opening directions, adaptation, feedback, conflict response, and stop signal for the segment. Live leadership or a complete written and rehearsed plan earns equal credit when it preserves each leadership decision; leading a group is not required.
masteryRule: Do not mark mastery from one session. Use safe participation, skill cues, tactical decisions, self-management, personal progress against the learner’s own stated task, and self-assessment — without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions separated by time or setting.
remediation: Return to the simplest version of organizing an activity that includes mixed abilities by design — slower, smaller range, closer target, or seated — then rebuild.

adaptiveRoutes.action: Return to the simplest version of organizing an activity that includes mixed abilities by design — slower, smaller range, closer target, or seated — then rebuild.
Ask the learner to explain the cue or tactic behind organizing an activity that includes mixed abilities by design before adding intensity or complexity.
Confirm the specific cue that worked, offer one varied application of organizing an activity that includes mixed abilities by design, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable movement pattern neutrally, contrast it with the critical features, and schedule varied practice.

adaptiveRoutes.signal: pain, dizziness, breathlessness, or head impact
adaptiveRoutes.action: Stop immediately, tell an adult, and do not resume in this session. This is never recorded as a failed attempt.

Offer the adapted, seated, solo, or described version of organizing an activity that includes mixed abilities by design; the alternate route is full credit when it supplies the stated transfer evidence and is not logged as a refusal. Full transfer credit requires the opening directions, adaptation, feedback, conflict response, and stop signal for the segment. Live leadership or a complete written and rehearsed plan earns equal credit when it preserves each leadership decision; leading a group is not required.

adaptiveRoutes.signal: transfer condition is too much today
adaptiveRoutes.action: Drop back to the first-pass version of organizing an activity that includes mixed abilities by design for this session and re-attempt the added demand on a later occasion. Reducing the demand is the correct response and is scored as full participation, but it does not itself satisfy the transfer evidence requirement.

Require accurate independent performance or description plus explanation on a later occasion or in a different setting before marking organizing an activity that includes mixed abilities by design mastered.

guardianOrParentVisibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose body data, fitness scores, photographs, video, recordings, or comparisons with other learners. For safety-critical units, record only the guardian confirmation that was required.

guardianSafetyReview.environment: Space appropriate to the planned segment.
guardianSafetyReview.movement_hazards: Depends on the planned segment; the leader is responsible for the safety check.
guardianSafetyReview.supervision_note: Guardian approves the segment plan and any participants involved.

safetyAndPrivacyNotes: Use respectful, non-shaming language about bodies, ability, and effort.
Allow a pause, rest, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, self-management, consistency, and reflection — never body size, weight, weight change, body composition, appearance, or comparison with another person.
Do not require weight, BMI, body-fat, body measurement, fitness-test norms, percentile ranks, calorie counts, or diet goals at any point.
Do not require a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as evidence; described, written, and demonstrated-to-one-adult evidence is the intended route.
Do not require performance in front of an audience, a group, or spectators.
Feedback language is explicitly constrained to performance and effort; commenting on a participant’s body, size, or appearance is taught as a failure of the leadership standard.
